title: English basics
about: The most common words of written and spoken English (wordfreq counts, grouped by dictionary word with tools/course/en/rank_en.py), most common first, 50 to a unit. Names of people and places are left out. Each word has a short, simple meaning in English and one short everyday sentence in American English that uses it the way native speakers do; ⟦ ⟧ marks the word in the sentence.

words.meaning: used before a noun when we know which one we mean
to exist; used to say what or where someone or something is (am, is, are, was, were)
in the direction of a place or person; also used before a verb (to eat)
words.sentence: I walk to school every day.

words.meaning: one; used before a singular noun (an before a vowel sound: an apple)
joins two words or ideas; also
belonging to; showing a part or an amount (a cup of tea)
words.sentence: I'd like a cup of coffee.

words.meaning: inside; during (in June)
words.sentence: The keys are in my bag.

words.meaning: the person who is speaking (me, my, myself)
the person or thing over there, or the one already mentioned (plural: those)
the thing or animal we are talking about; also used for the weather and time
the person or people someone is talking to
to own or hold something; to eat or drink (have lunch) (has, had)
meant to be given to someone; for a purpose; during a time (for two hours)
touching the top of something; on a day (on Monday)
words.sentence: Your phone is on the table.

words.meaning: the one here, near me (plural: these)
together with someone or something; using something
to carry out an action; also used to make questions and negatives (does, did, done)
words.sentence: I do my homework after school.

words.meaning: in the job or role of; in the same way (as fast as)
a man or boy who has already been mentioned (him, his)
in or near a place; at a time (at six)
